23761-little-journeys-to-the-homes-of-th.title: Little Journeys to the Homes of Eminent Orators
23761-little-journeys-to-the-homes-of-th.creator: Elbert Hubbard
23761-little-journeys-to-the-homes-of-th.description: A book by Elbert Hubbard. Once upon a day there was a grocer who lived in Indianapolis, Indiana. The grocer's name being Heinrich Schliemann, his nationality can be inferred; and as for pedigree, it is enough to state that his ancestors did not land at either Plymouth or Jamestown. However, he was an American citizen.

arxiv-2205-12308.title: Non-split supermanifolds associated with the cotangent bundle
arxiv-2205-12308.creator: Arkady Onishchik
arxiv-2205-12308.description: Abstract Here, I study the problem of classification of non-split supermanifolds having as retract the split supermanifold ( M , Ω ) (M,\Omega) , where Ω \Omega is the sheaf of holomorphic forms on a given complex manifold M M of dimension > 1 >1 .

arxiv-2205-13776.title: PrivacyDates: A Framework for More Privacy-Preserving Timestamp Data Types
arxiv-2205-13776.creator: Christian Burkert and Jonathan Balack and Hannes Federrath
arxiv-2205-13776.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christian Burkert and Jonathan Balack and Hannes Federrath. Case studies of application software data models indicate that timestamps are excessively used in connection with user activity. This contradicts the principle of data minimisation which demands a limitation to data necessary for a given purpose. Prior work has also identified common purposes of timestamps that can be realised by more privacy-preserving alternatives like counters and dates with purpose-oriented precision. In this paper, we follow up by demonstrating the real-world applicability of those alternatives.

arxiv-2207-06398.title: A numerical study of stellar discs in galactic nuclei
arxiv-2207-06398.creator: Taras Panamarev, Bence Kocsis
arxiv-2207-06398.description: Abstract We explore the dynamics of stellar discs in the close vicinity of a supermassive black hole (SMBH) by means of direct N N -body simulations. We show that an isolated nuclear stellar disc exhibits anisotropic mass segregation meaning that massive stars settle to lower orbital inclinations and more circular orbits than the light stars.

arxiv-2207-12364.title: Confinement in de Sitter Space and the Swampland
arxiv-2207-12364.creator: Rashmish K. Mishra
arxiv-2207-12364.description: Abstract The relation between confinement scale Λ c \Lambda_{c} of a gauge theory and the Hubble scale H H of the background quasi de Sitter space, required to satisfy the Festina Lente criteria ( Λ c ≳ H \Lambda_{c}\gtrsim H ) from swampland principles, are investigated for a holographic theory using the Karch-Randall setup.

arxiv-2302-04327.title: A Lorentz-violating low-energy model for the bilayer Graphene
arxiv-2302-04327.creator: Y. M. P. Gomes, M. J. Neves
arxiv-2302-04327.description: Abstract In this work, we propose a model with Lorentz symmetry violation which describes the electronic low energy limit of the AA-bilayer graphene (BLG) system. The AA-type bilayer is known to preserve the linear dispersion relation of the graphene layer in the low energy limit.

arxiv-2309-06483.title: Percolation Transition in a Topological Phase
arxiv-2309-06483.creator: Saikat Mondal, Subrata Pachhal, Adhip Agarwala
arxiv-2309-06483.description: Abstract Transition out of a topological phase is typically characterized by discontinuous changes in topological invariants along with bulk gap closings. However, as a clean system is geometrically punctured, it is natural to ask the fate of an underlying topological phase.

arxiv-2402-09662.title: GeoBotsVR: A Robotics Learning Game for Beginners with Hands-on Learning Simulation DOI: 10.1145/3613905.3648111 Conference: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; May 11–16, 2024; Honolulu, HI, USA Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in
arxiv-2402-09662.creator: Syed Tanzim Mubarrat
arxiv-2402-09662.description: Abstract . This article introduces GeoBotsVR , an easily accessible virtual reality game that combines elements of puzzle-solving with robotics learning and aims to cultivate interest and motivation in robotics, programming, and electronics among individuals with limited experience in these domains.

arxiv-2410-15217.title: A Predictive Approach To Enhance Time-Series Forecasting
arxiv-2410-15217.creator: Skye Gunasekaran 1 , Assel Kembay 1 , Hugo Ladret 2 , Rui-Jie Zhu 1 , Laurent Perrinet 3 , Omid Kavehei 4 , Jason Eshraghian 1 1 Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of California, Santa Cruz, CA, USA 2 Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research, Basel, Switzerland
arxiv-2410-15217.description: Abstract Accurate time-series forecasting is crucial in various scientific and industrial domains, yet deep learning models often struggle to capture long-term dependencies and adapt to data distribution shifts over time. We introduce Future-Guided Learning, an approach that enhances time-series event forecasting through a dynamic feedback mechanism inspired by predictive coding.

arxiv-2410-18904.title: Modulated Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators for Temporal Interpolation of Weather Forecasts
arxiv-2410-18904.creator: Jussi Leinonen, Boris Bonev, Thorsten Kurth, Yair Cohen
arxiv-2410-18904.description: Abstract Weather and climate data are often available at limited temporal resolution, either due to storage limitations, or in the case of weather forecast models based on deep learning, their inherently long time steps. The coarse temporal resolution makes it difficult to capture rapidly evolving weather events.

arxiv-2509-25837.title: Distillation of Large Language Models via Concrete Score Matching
arxiv-2509-25837.creator: Yeongmin Kim, Donghyeok Shin, Mina Kang, Byeonghu Na, Il-Chul Moon
arxiv-2509-25837.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) deliver remarkable performance but are costly to deploy, motivating knowledge distillation (KD) for efficient inference. Existing KD objectives typically match student and teacher probabilities via softmax, which blurs valuable logit information. While direct logit distillation (DLD) mitigates softmax smoothing, it fails to account for logit shift invariance, thereby restricting the solution space.

europmc-pmc3794996.creator: Tong S, Zhu X, Li Y, Shi M, Zhang J, Bourgeois M, Yang H, Chen X, Recuenco S, Gomez J, Chen LM, Johnson A, Tao Y, Dreyfus C, Yu W, McBride R, Carney PJ, Gilbert AT, Chang J, Guo Z, Davis CT, Paulson JC, Stevens J, Rupprecht CE, Holmes EC, Wilson IA, Donis RO.
europmc-pmc3794996.description: Aquatic birds harbor diverse influenza A viruses and are a major viral reservoir in nature. pmc-11604479.title: The penetration of therapeutics across the blood-brain barrier: Classic case studies and clinical implications
pmc-11604479.creator: William A Banks, Elizabeth M Rhea, May J Reed, Michelle A Erickson
pmc-11604479.description: SummaryThe blood-brain barrier (BBB) plays central roles in the maintenance and health of the brain. Its mechanisms to safeguard the brain against xenobiotics and endogenous toxins also make the BBB the primary obstacle to the development of drugs for the central nervous system (CNS). Here, we review classic examples of the intersection of clinical medicine, drug delivery, and the BBB.

pmc-12534416.title: Exploring colostrum microbiota and its influence on early calf gut microbiota development using full-length 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding
pmc-12534416.creator: Leire Urrutia‑Angulo, Medelin Ocejo, Timur Yergaliyev, Beatriz Oporto, Gorka Aduriz, Amélia Camarinha-Silva, Ana Hurtado
pmc-12534416.description: The early gut microbiota of calves is seeded by colostrum and shaped by diet, environment, disease, and antibiotic treatments. This study analyzed the colostrum microbiota of 42 cows and tracked their calves’ gut microbiota during early life (days d1, d16, and d57), assessing the impact of antimicrobial dry cow therapy and infection treatments.

pmc-12633751.description: The current study used a culture-independent methodology to investigate the rumen microbiome composition in two genetically divergent groups of spring-calving dairy cows, high (€218) and low (€157) Economic Breeding Index (EBI), grazing two sward treatments—perennial ryegrass (grass-only) or perennial ryegrass and white clover (grass-clover)—at three time points across spring, summer, and autumn of a single grazing season.

pmc-12798441.title: Burnout among public health physicians and residents in Canada following the COVID-19 pandemic: A cross-sectional study
pmc-12798441.creator: Syeda Aiman Fatima, Xi Yu Hao, Diana Sun, Itai Malkin, Elizabeth Alvarez, Laura N. Anderson, David Edward-Ooi Poon, Japteg Singh, Emma Apatu, Chris P. Verschoor, Thomas Piggott, Emily Belita, Sheila A. Boamah, Arielle Sutton, Zayya Zendo, Jessica P. Hopkins
pmc-12798441.description: Previous research identified high levels of burnout in the Canadian public health workforce during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study presents the prevalence of burnout, associated participant demographic and workplace characteristics, and associated secondary outcomes among Canadian public health physicians and residents one year after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-13246725.title: Disease-associated RNA and protein signatures in iPSC-derived microglia model of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13246725.creator: Wenzhe Wu, Eun Seok Choi, Luke Liu, Veena Thamilselvan, Le Li, Meagan D. Rippee-Brooks, Kashish Khatkar, Dar-Yin Li, Denise McGrath, Aidan Manning, Sergio Barberan-Soler, Inhan Lee, Yingxin Zhao, Xiang Fang, Xiaoyong Bao
pmc-13246725.description: IntroductionMicroglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, play a critical role in maintaining neural homeostasis and regulating inflammatory responses in the brain. Increasing evidence suggests that microglial dysfunction contributes to the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these alterations remain incompletely understood.
